newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks hold ground in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks hold ground in quiet trade.

text.p: SPI Futures 2631.0 +7.0 US 30yr cl 6.87 -0.04
10yrbond futs 92.655 unch Gold NY 347.10 Lon fix 343.55
AUD US$0.7600 (local $0.7602) CRB Index cl 248.44 -0.20
*Stocks end slightly higher in quiet trade as market awaits fresh direction. Volume 378.7 million, A$974.1 million value, 1,138 stocks traded, 341 steady, 412 up, 385 down.
The Australian stock market held a small gain all afternoon to the close on Wednesday, with little fresh news to drive a six-week rally to higher levels.

The All Ordinaries Index pushed up about 10 points in late morning trade, but soon settled back to end the day 2.3 points higher at 2,615.9 in quiet trade. "For the next few days there doesn't seem to be anything around the corner that will drive the market aggressively higher," said David Iron, head of institutional sales at HSBC James Capel Australia.

The June share price index futures contract closed 7.0 points higher at 2631.0, a 15.1 point premium to the underlying index. Brokers said the possibility of a further official interest rate cut, which boosted the market on Friday and Monday, appeared to have eased.

Weaker commodity prices had also taken some of the gloss of the resources sector, with the mining index coming back about 0.4 percent on the day. "A week or two ago people were feeling a lot better about resources," Iron said.

The Reserve Bank board met on Tuesday morning but, as expected, announced no change in policy, while official data showing a 0.9 percent rise in gross domestic product in the March quarter had no impact on stocks.

Bottler Coca-Cola Amatil posted one of the strongest gains for the day, after it had reached final agreement on a share swap deal with San Miguel Corp to acquire the Philippine group's soft drink operations.
C-C Amatil closed on its highs at A$16.10, a 70 cent gain, although dealers said the rise may have been partly technical, as index-based portfolios chased shares.
The difficulty arises because C-C Amatil's index weighting is based on the entire number of shares on issue, but about 58 percent will be held by The Coca-Cola Co and San Miguel Corp.
The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) topped turnover with 18.9 million shares changing hands after going ex-dividend 22 cents. ANZ closed down 24 cents at A$8.88.
Among other banks, the Commonwealth Bank of Australia retraced recent losses to add 31 cents to A$14.27, while the other two big banks were slightly firmer.

Queensland's so-called Rundle twins, Central Pacific Minerals and Southern Pacific Petroleum, rose sharply after announcing an agreement with financiers to proceed with stage one of the Stuart shale oil deposit.
In the building sector, James Hardie continued its recent run adding another five cents to A$4.20 ahead of the release of its annual result on Thursday.
Bellwether Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd added 10 cents to A$18.97, while News Ltd fell 15 cents to A$5.71.

In other markets, 10-year T-bonds ended unchanged 92.655 after rates were left unchanged, while the Australian dollar lost early support to drift to US$0.7595 by 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT) from US$0.7597 late on Tuesday.
